# IconButton

## Description
It runs one action drawn as a single glyph, and its `title` is both its accessible name and the hint a sighted person reads.

`import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";`, source `src/ui/IconButton.tsx`, status `ready`.
Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/button-icon-name, trap/icon-optical-size, trap/icon-optical-align, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight.

### Foundation
Not applicable: hand-rolled — the circle, the .08 hover fill and the 14px glyph are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (`docs/system/decisions.md`), and the glyphs are the app's own `src/icons.ts` paths.

## Examples
`<IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />` — the panel's close control.

Real uses, 34 call sites (`rg -c "<IconButton" src` → `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:18`, `src/components/BenchPanel.tsx:1`, `src/components/InlineAsk.tsx:1`, `src/components/LayerManager.tsx:1`, `src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1`, `src/components/Menu.tsx:1`, `src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1`, `src/components/ToolStrip.tsx:1`, `src/components/TopBar.tsx:3`):
- `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx` — the close on a chip of `@` context in the composer card (`sm`), as the selection chip's. Added 2026-11-12.
- `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx` — the composer pilot: the toolbar's attach (`soft`), stop and send (`inverted`), and each attachment chip's remove circle (`sm`).
- `src/components/BenchPanel.tsx` — the bench section's fold key (`sm`, `expanded`, `controls`), as the layers' and the properties' sections fold. Added 2026-11-12.
- `src/components/InlineAsk.tsx` — the inline ask's send (`inverted`, `sm`, `shortcut="Enter"`), off while the line is empty with the reason as its `description`. Added 2026-11-12.
- `src/components/ToolStrip.tsx:295` — every tool of the ribbon's compact row (a window of a phone's width): the glyph from the tool's icon id, the title its label and shortcut, click to invoke it; and the key at the tab row's end that folds the tool band (`expanded`, `controls`). On a wider window a tool is the ghost `Button` with its glyph over its label.

## Variants

### variant
- `ghost`: the transparent circle for a tool bar; the default. Used at 21 call sites (the assistant header's New chat and Close, the setup sheet's show-or-hide key beside the API key, the narrow window's Main menu key, the sidebar sections' fold and unfold (the layers and the properties), the title bar's sidebar and command-line keys, the changes row's show and hide, an attachment chip's remove, the selection chip's remove, the turn's copy, a tool's code copy, a reply's code copy, a failed request's Try again, a queued message's send and remove, the composer's attach, every tool in the tool strip, and the top bar's assistant key).
- `soft`: the resting `.08` fill, for a tool that is currently on. Used at 1 call site (the transcript's jump-to-latest key).
- `inverted`: the ink-coloured circle with the accent-surface glyph, for the one primary action. Used at 2 call sites (the composer's stop and send).

## States
| State | Trigger | What the user can do | Shown by, besides color | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rest | Nothing is over the circle. | Click it, or Tab to it. | The variant's resting fill, or none on `ghost`. | by hand |
| Hover | The pointer is over the circle, on a device with a hover pointer. | Click it. | The fill steps up one rung; the cursor is a pointer. | by hand |
| Pressed | The pointer is held down. | Release to run the action. | The next fill rung up. | by hand |
| Focused | Keyboard focus arrives by Tab. | Enter or Space runs the action. | The 1px ring in the focus ink at offset -1, following the circle; on `inverted`, the ring is the glyph's ink drawn 3px inside the edge. | by hand |
| Selected | The caller passes `selected` (a toggle). | Click it again to turn the tool off. | The `.08` fill squared to the control radius (a resting key has no fill and a hovered one a round fill), the full ink, and `aria-pressed="true"`. | test |
| Expanded | The caller passes `expanded` (a fold key), with `controls` naming the region. | Click it to fold the region away; click again to bring it back. | `aria-expanded="true"` while the region shows and `"false"` while it is folded, and `aria-controls` holding the region's `id`; the look is the variant's own. | test |
| Hinted | A mouse or a pen rests on the circle for 0.4s (at once when another hint was up within the last 0.3s), or keyboard focus arrives. Never a finger. | Read the name; a press, a click or Escape puts the box away, and it stays away until the pointer or the focus moves to another control. | The layer's hint box holding the `title`, its shortcut as a key cap and the `description` on a second line, below the circle (above it at the window's foot), held inside the window's edges. | test |
| Disabled | The caller's condition is false. | Tab to it and read its hint: the name, and why it is blocked when the caller passes `description`. No click by pointer, Enter or Space, and no hover fill. | The glyph drops to the disabled ink; the fill to the disabled step; `aria-disabled="true"`. | test |

Example: A blocked tool at the disabled ink. (`docs/system/examples/icon-button/disabled.tsx`)

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

/** Disabled, and still reachable: the hint names the key and `description` says why it is blocked. */
export default function Disabled() {
  return <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled description="Type a message first" />;
}
```

Example: A toggled tool: the full ink on the .08 fill, squared, announced pressed. (`docs/system/examples/icon-button/selected.tsx`)

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function Selected() {
  return <IconButton icon="list" title="List view" selected />;
}
```

Example: A fold key over the region it folds, announced expanded. (`docs/system/examples/icon-button/expanded.tsx`)

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function Expanded() {
  return (
    <section>
      <IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title="Hide the layers" expanded controls="layers-body" />
      <div id="layers-body">Outline, Center, Hidden</div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

### State precedence
- Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the circle; hover only steps the fill.
- Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled circle keeps its resting look under the pointer and takes no click.
- Selected and Hover: both show. The squared `.08` selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds the pointer cursor and nothing to the fill.
- Selected and Expanded: Not applicable: a key is a toggle or a fold key, never both; the caller passes one of the two props.
- Expanded and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled fold key keeps `aria-expanded` and takes no click.
- Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled toggle drops to the disabled ink and takes no click.
- Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the circle is held down.
- Hinted and Pressed: Pressed wins. The press puts the hint away.
- Hinted and Hover: both show. The hint follows the hover after its delay.
- Hinted and Focused: both show. The hint arrives with the ring, with no delay.
- Hinted and Selected: both show. The hint names a toggle whatever its state.
- Hinted and Expanded: both show on a fold key, until the click that folds puts the hint away; on a key with `popup`, Expanded wins, and the hint stays away while the key's own menu or dialog is open.
- Hinted and Disabled: both show. A disabled key still says what it is, and why it is blocked when it has a `description`.
- Focused and Disabled: both show. A disabled key takes focus and the ring, so a keyboard user can reach its hint; Enter and Space do nothing.

### Motion
| Trigger | Kind | Preset | Properties | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The pointer enters or leaves | input | hover / focus feedback (`--dur-fast` + `--ease-standard`) | background-color, color | The fill and the ink change at once: the shell's `:root[data-animations="off"] *` rule removes the transition. |
| The pointer is held down | input | press (`--dur-press` + `--ease-standard`) | transform | The circle stays at rest: the shell's `:root[data-animations="off"] *` rule removes the transition. |
| The pointer presses down | input | hover / focus feedback (`--dur-fast` + `--ease-standard`) | background-color | The fill changes at once, by the same rule. |

## Props

<!-- Props generated from src/ui/IconButton.tsx with TypeScript by scripts/props-table.mjs -->
| Prop | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `string` |  | The id from `../icons.ts`; the glyph is drawn in code. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The accessible name (`aria-label`) and the hint's text. |
| `controls?` | `string` |  | The `id` of the region a fold key shows and hides: sets `aria-controls`. |
| `description?` | `string` |  | A second line under the name in the hint, and the key's accessible description: why it is disabled ("Type a message first"), what it will do. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` |  | Blocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink. |
| `expanded?` | `boolean` |  | A fold key: sets `aria-expanded` to whether the region it folds is showing now. |
| `onClick?` | `((event: MouseEvent) => void)` |  | Runs on click. |
| `popup?` | `IconButtonPopup` |  | The key opens a popup of this kind: sets `aria-haspopup`. |
| `selected?` | `boolean` |  | A toggle-style icon button: sets `aria-pressed`, and while on draws the full ink on the `.08` fill, squared to the control radius (not the round `.14` disc it was until 2026-11-11). |
| `shortcut?` | `string` |  | The shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it ("Ctrl+Z", "F9"): a key cap in the hint and `aria-keyshortcuts` on the button. |
| `size?` | `IconButtonSize` |  | The box size. |
| `variant?` | `IconButtonVariant` |  | The look. |

- `icon`: the id from `src/icons.ts`; the glyph is drawn in code, never an image.
- `title`: the accessible name (`aria-label`) and the text of the layer's hint; an icon alone has no name without it. No native `title` attribute is rendered.
- `variant`: the look; defaults to `ghost`.
- `size`: the circle; `md` is 24px with a 14px glyph, `sm` is 20px with a 12px glyph.
- `selected`: sets `aria-pressed` and the selected look: the full ink on the `.08` fill, squared to `--radius-control`. It is the one selected recipe, in every variant; until 2026-11-11 it was the `.14` fill at the round radius, which in the title bar (its 3 call sites, 2 on at rest) drew filled discs louder than the title (`docs/system/decisions.md`, "The quiet pass"). A `soft` button rests on the same `.08` fill, so a selected `soft` one is told by its square corner and its ink alone: pick `ghost` for a key that toggles.
- `expanded`: a fold key; sets `aria-expanded` to whether the region it folds is showing.
- `controls`: the `id` of the region a fold key shows and hides, or of the popup a key opens; sets `aria-controls`.
- `popup`: the key opens a popup of this kind; sets `aria-haspopup`. `menu` for a list of actions, `listbox` for a list of values to pick one from, `dialog` for a popover holding fields or other controls.
- `shortcut`: the shortcut that runs the same action, as the user reads it (`Ctrl+Z`, `F9`): a key cap after the name in the hint, and `aria-keyshortcuts` on the button. A `title` that ends in the shortcut in brackets ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)") still draws the cap; its name keeps the bracket, so no `aria-keyshortcuts` repeats it.
- `description`: a second line under the name in the hint, tied to the button as its accessible description (`aria-describedby`): why the key is disabled, what it will do. Never the name.
- `disabled`: blocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink. It sets `aria-disabled="true"`, never the native `disabled`, so the key stays in the Tab order and under the pointer and its hint still shows.
- `onClick`: runs on click; a disabled circle never fires it.

## Usage

### When to use
- The action is one glyph a tooltip can name: close, attach, send, stop, add.
- The control sits in a tool bar, a panel header or a toolbar row where a label would crowd the row.

### When not to use
- The action needs a label to be understood. Use `Button` instead.
- The control is a list item with a name. Use `Row` instead.
- The glyph is a status rather than an action. Use `Chip` instead.

### Rules
- `rule/icon-button-name`: When an icon button is rendered, pass `title` for every use, because the glyph alone leaves the accessible name empty and a screen reader announces "button". Evidence: app 3/3 composer icon buttons, `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx`. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<IconButton icon="close" />` — no name.
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />`
- `rule/icon-button-one-inverted`: When a toolbar row holds icon buttons, keep at most 1 `inverted` circle, because the ink-coloured circle is the row's primary action and a second one splits the eye. Evidence: measured 1 inverted send button in the composer toolbar, `docs/system/decisions.md`. Check: review `src/ui/ui.css`.
  - Don't: two `variant="inverted"` circles in the composer row.
  - Do: 1 `inverted` send and `ghost` for attach and stop.
- `rule/icon-button-fold-expanded`: When an icon button folds and unfolds a region, pass `expanded` with the region's state and `controls` with the region's `id`, and leave `selected` unset, because a title that flips between Show and Hide is the only signal otherwise, and a screen reader hears 2 unrelated buttons where there is 1 key that is collapsed or expanded. Evidence: app 3/3 fold keys (the layers, the properties, the changes row), `src/components/LayersPanel.tsx`. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} selected={open()} />`
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="chevron-down" size="sm" title={open() ? "Hide the layers" : "Show the layers"} expanded={open()} controls="layers-body" />`

- `rule/icon-button-popup-kind`: When an icon button opens something that floats over the page, pass `popup` with its kind (1 of `menu`, `listbox`, `dialog`, matching the `role` of what opens), `expanded` with whether it is open, and `controls` with its `id` while it is rendered, and leave `selected` unset, because a key with no `aria-haspopup` is announced as a plain button and the menu it opens arrives unannounced. Evidence: single use `src/components/MenuBar.tsx:194`, the narrow window's Main menu key, which sets the attribute from outside on mount. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" expanded={open()} />` with `setAttribute("aria-haspopup", "menu")` on mount.
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="list" title="Main menu" popup="menu" expanded={open()} controls={open() ? "main-menu" : undefined} />`
- `rule/icon-button-no-native-title`: When an icon button is styled or wrapped, add 0 hints of its own (no `title` attribute set from outside, no `Tooltip` around it), because the component already shows its `title` in the layer's hint box and a second hint stacks on the first. Evidence: app 31/31 icon buttons in the running shell render no `title` attribute, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<Tooltip text="Close"><IconButton icon="close" title="Close" /></Tooltip>`
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />`
- `rule/icon-button-shortcut-prop`: When an icon button's action has a shortcut, pass it as `shortcut` and keep it out of `title`, because the hint draws it as 1 key cap and the button says it through `aria-keyshortcuts`, while a bracket in the title puts "(Ctrl+Z)" into the accessible name a speech-input user has to say; the parsed bracket form stays for a caller that has not moved, and no call site in the app uses it now (the tool strip's five, the title bar's three and the composer's send and stop pass `shortcut`). Evidence: app 9/31 icon buttons in the running shell carry a shortcut in brackets in their name, measured in the browser 2026-11-11. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo (Ctrl+Z)" />`
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="undo" title="Undo" shortcut="Ctrl+Z" />`
- `rule/icon-button-disabled-reason`: When an icon button is disabled by something the user can fix, pass the reason as `description` in 1 short sentence, because the disabled key stays focusable and hoverable for exactly this, and its name alone says what it is and 0 words about why it is dead. Evidence: single use `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:977`, the composer's send key, disabled while the message is empty with no reason given. Check: test `src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} />`
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="send" title="Send" disabled={empty()} description={empty() ? "Type a message first" : undefined} />`

### Content
- `rule/icon-button-title-sentence`: When `title` is written, name the action in sentence case with no full stop (Close the panel, Send, Stop), because the same string is the hint and the accessible name. Evidence: single use `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:920`, the "Attach a picture (or paste, or drop one)" label. Check: review `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx`.
  - Don't: `title="close panel."`
  - Do: `title="Close the panel"`

### Anti-slop
- `rule/icon-button-canonical-element`: When a surface needs an icon action, render `IconButton` rather than a raw `<button>` with a hand-sized glyph, because the replaced classes hard-code 3 different box sizes and their own hover opacities. Evidence: app 10/10 lines across `src/assistant.css` and `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx`, `rg -c "assistant-icon|assistant-attachment-x" src`. Check: review `src/ui/IconButton.tsx`.
  - Don't: `<button class="assistant-icon" onClick={stop}>…</button>`
  - Do: `<IconButton icon="stop" title="Stop" onClick={stop} />`

### Limits
- `rule/icon-button-row-limit`: When a toolbar row holds more than 5 icon buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer row holds 3 at 24px each with 4px gaps and the row starts crowding the input past 5. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px with 4px gaps, `docs/system/decisions.md`. Check: review `src/components/AssistantPane.tsx`.
  - Don't: 6 circles in the composer's toolbar row.
  - Do: 3 circles in the row and the rest inside a menu.
- `rule/icon-button-touch-target`: When 2 `sm` icon buttons sit side by side, keep at least 4px between them, because under a coarse pointer each 20px circle keeps its drawn size and takes a 24px target from an invisible `::after` 2px past every edge, and closer circles overlap their targets. Evidence: measured 20px circle with a 24px `::after` target, `src/ui/ui.css:1558`. Check: review `src/ui/ui.css`.
  - Don't: `.my-row .ui-icon-button--sm + .ui-icon-button--sm { margin-left: 0 }` — two 24px targets on a 20px pitch.
  - Do: `.my-row { display: flex; gap: var(--gap-4) }`

## Accessibility
Rests on the native `<button>` element, with the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech. Disabled is the layer's own, shared with `Button`: `aria-disabled="true"` with the click refused on the button itself, because the native `disabled` takes a key out of the Tab order and, in some of the system webviews the desktop app runs in, out of the pointer's reach, and a key nobody can reach cannot say what it is or why it is blocked (`docs/system/decisions.md`, "Disabled controls").

### Keyboard
| Key | Where focus is | Effect | Focus after | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tab | The circle, in document order. | Moves focus to it; the accent ring draws and the hint shows at once. | On the circle. | by hand |
| Enter | The focused circle. | Runs the action. | Stays on the circle. | test |
| Space | The focused circle. | Runs the action on release, exactly once. | Stays on the circle. | by hand |
| Tab (disabled) | A disabled circle, in document order. | Moves focus to it, as to any key; the ring draws and its hint shows at once. | On the circle. | by hand |
| Enter or Space (disabled) | The focused disabled circle. | Nothing: the click is refused before any handler hears it. | Stays on the circle. | test |
| Escape | The focused or hovered circle, its hint showing. | Puts the hint away; the key is not consumed, so a surface that closes on Escape still closes. | Stays on the circle. | test |

### ARIA
| Part | Role | Accessible name from | States and properties | Announced | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The circle | `button` (native) | `aria-label` (the `title` string) | `aria-pressed` when `selected`; `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on a fold key; `aria-haspopup` with `aria-expanded` on a key that opens a popup; `aria-keyshortcuts` with `shortcut`; `aria-describedby` pointing at the `description`'s words; `aria-disabled="true"` when blocked | "Close the panel, button" / "Stop, pressed button" / "Hide the layers, expanded, button" / "Main menu, menu button, collapsed" | test |
| The hint | None: the box is `aria-hidden="true"` | — | It repeats the circle's name for the eye; assistive tech reads the name from `aria-label` | Nothing | test |
| The glyph | `svg` with `aria-hidden="true"` | — | Hidden from the accessibility tree | Nothing: the name is the button's | test |

## Tokens

## Related
- `Button`: when the action needs a visible label.
- `Chip`: when the glyph and the text are a fact rather than an action.
- `Row`: when the clickable band is a list item.
- `Tab`: when the control brings one view of a strip to the front rather than toggling a setting; a closable tab draws its own close key.
- `Tooltip`: the hint box this component shows by itself; wrap another control in it, never this one.
- `Kbd`: the key cap the hint draws for a shortcut.
- `Checkbox`: when the on/off belongs to a form's value rather than to a tool.
- `Toggle`: when a setting is switched in place under a fixed name, its state drawn by the glyph and never by a fill: a list row's state keys, a bar's drafting settings.
